messages.author: d718c6bb1db28db2
messages.subject: Re: adjusting line length and total area surveyed when effort is
parts:
Magaly, it is a judgement call which you do. The problem with missing
effort is that it isn't missing at random. If you assume it is, then
you just reduce the line length and proceed as normal. If the missing
effort might be correlated with animal density, then you would want to
exclude the region that effort represents from your study area, as it
was unsurveyed. You then estimate density and abundance for the
remaining area. In this case, it is difficult sometimes to say what
part of your intended study area corresponds to the missing effort.
With a parallel line design, the easy way to define it is to say that it
extends halfway to the next line. If you only delete the area in the
strip, then you again end up with unbalanced survey area through your
study region, and if the density around the missing strips is not
average, then you will get bias.

Conceptually, I don't think there is any difference between effort
missing through fog and effort missing through technical problems,
except perhaps in scale. If fog caused you to miss only short sections
of line, and affected only a small percentage of total effort, then the
first solution of just shortening your lines appropriately makes sense.
If the technical problem caused you to miss an extensive part of your
study area, then the only sensible option is to reduce your study area
to the area where you do have data - i.e. the second solution.

Steve Buckland

Magaly CHAMBELLANT wrote:
> > Good Day,
> >
> > When surveying seals on ice, we sometimes flew over patches of fog (no visibility) or we encountered technical problems with the recorders and lost data on parts of some lines.
> > While attending the workshop in Petaluma last September, I mentioned this problem to one of the instructor and I thought I understood the answer...but it seems I was wrong. Here is what I have in my notes, that now seems confusing to me:
> >
> > 1) for fog: no visibility so no effort; the line length should be decreased by the parts with fog but total area surveyed should remain the same
> > 2) for technical problems: remove effort by decreasing line length AND corresponding area from the total area surveyed as followed: (strip width*lenght of line were no data was recorded)+area corresponding to half way to the next line
> >
> > Why shouldn't I adjust the total area for fog? Why should I remove more area (i.e. half-way to the next line) than the strip surveyed in case of technical problems?
> >
> > Thank you in advance for your help,
> >
